title: Days sales outstanding deterioration
question: Calculate days sales outstanding (year-end trade receivables divided by revenue, multiplied by 365) for both years. What happened, and what does it mean for cash?

key_figures.label: Approximate cash tied up by the extra 15 days

gold_answer.summary: DSO rose from 45.0 to 60.0 days, an increase of 15 days. Receivables grew 46.7% while revenue grew only 10.0%, so the increase is not explained by sales growth: customers are taking longer to pay. At FY2025 revenue of about GBP 22k per day, the extra 15 days ties up roughly GBP 330k of cash.
gold_answer.main_driver: Collections slowed: receivables grew more than four times faster than revenue.

design_note: Baseline. Formula given in the question. Tests whether the model links the ratio to a cash consequence, and whether it rules out revenue growth as the explanation. The table does not say why customers are paying later, so any stated reason is a grounding failure.
